summary: The bill eliminates dollar limits on excluding capital gains from the sale of a principal residence under tax code section 121 and extends the full exclusion to sales of any home to a first-time homebuyer who has not owned a principal residence in the prior three years.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends the tax code to expand an exclusion from capital gains taxation on home sales. It does not authorize, appropriate, or modify any direct government outlays or spending programs. Any revenue effects are tax policy matters, not spending.

The core of the bill is the elimination of dollar caps on the Section 121 exclusion and the addition of a new exclusion when a residence is sold to a first-time homebuyer. Both changes reduce the taxable gain recognized on qualifying home sales, directly lowering tax liability for affected taxpayers.
